mutations.because: Emit the whole allocation history instead of the live slots. This is the recreate-on-delete bug wearing the new code's clothes: a tombstoned slot is drawn (which it must be, or the survivors above it move) and then handed out again, so the deleted creative comes back at its old index with its old seed and its old axes. Nothing else in the run can tell it apart from a creative that was never deleted.
command: deleting a slot leaves every other creative byte-identical

mutations.because: Draw the recipe's cardinality rather than the slots actually allocated. The two are equal for every brief that carries no occupancy, so the whole pre-SL2 suite stays green — which is the point: this mutation is invisible until a creative is ADDED, and then the added slot is never drawn at all. `nextIndex` is the monotonic cursor, and reading `count` instead is the same category error as the compaction it replaced.
command: an added creative takes a fresh index above every index ever used

mutations.because: Stop distancing a candidate against the slots already allocated — SL-D4's whole subject. Appending one creative to seven would then accept the first point drawn, including one that duplicates an existing creative exactly, and the operator gets two identical pictures at two slots. `conflicts` takes a pair for this reason; a draw that never consults the occupants is the old "plan a fresh set" behaviour with a new name.
command: an appended creative is distanced against the occupants

mutations.because: Gate the exhaustive fallback on "no tombstones" rather than on "the allocation target is still the recipe's count". It is the plausible reading — protect the occupants by refusing to re-choose the set — and it is wrong in the direction that matters: a DELETE leaves `nextIndex` alone, so the search is asked the identical question and returns the identical set, and skipping it strands every brief whose plan needed it (the reported tight motion case reaches 8 of 8 only through this path). Deleting one creative would refuse the whole run.
command: a delete on a brief that needed the exhaustive search also keeps its survivors
